Flooding Disrupts Automotive Supply Chains in Bangladesh, Impacting ACI Ltd Operations

Severe monsoon flooding in Bangladesh has disrupted operations across the country’s automotive industry, with major assembly plants, parts suppliers, and transport routes affected. The floods, triggered by days of torrential rain since early this week, have inundated several industrial zones in the Dhaka and Chattogram regions, causing immediate concerns over production targets and delivery schedules.

ACI Ltd confirmed on Thursday that its primary assembly plant in Narayanganj remains partially closed due to water ingress and ongoing safety checks. “We are working around the clock to clear floodwater from critical areas and resume safe operations, but the situation is still evolving,” said Tanvir Alam, head of operations at ACI Ltd. “Our first priority is the safety of our workers, followed by stabilizing our supply and distribution chains.”

Industry insiders report that at least four major automotive components suppliers have halted deliveries after floodwaters submerged access roads and rendered several warehouse sites inaccessible. One such supplier, Delta Auto Components, indicated that its Rajshahi distribution hub has been cut off since Tuesday, with more than 70% of its outbound shipments delayed. “We are coordinating with logistics partners to reroute shipments, but highway closures are causing significant backlogs,” stated Delta’s logistics manager, Mohammad Harun.

According to the Bangladesh Automotive Manufacturers Association, the floods threaten to delay vehicle assembly and component imports by one to two weeks if conditions do not improve soon. “With key arterial roads underwater and several regional ports operating at reduced capacity, the movement of both finished vehicles and critical parts has slowed to a crawl,” said association spokesperson Farhana Rahman.

Union representatives have expressed concern over lost wages for daily workers unable to reach flooded plants. “We urge management to provide support for affected employees during this difficult time,” said Shafiqul Islam, union leader at a major plant.

As monsoon rains persist, industry stakeholders are monitoring the situation closely and assessing long-term risks to supply chain resilience.
